Do not file the CUA application or pay any fees until Planning confirms in writing that a feasible approval path exists.

items.original_text: Filing step: If Planning confirms that a Type 42 from within the SUD is required and available, engage an ABC license broker to locate and escrow a Type 42 license currently held by a bar inside the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD boundaries. What to say: Provide the broker with the SUD boundary shapefile (Planning Code § 249.60 map) and instruct them to search only for Type 42 licenses at bar addresses within those boundaries. Confirm the license's status (active, no disciplinary holds), the transfer timeline, and the asking price. Make the lease contingent on Planning's CUA approval and ABC's transfer approval. Do not close escrow on the license until the CUA is granted and the ABC application is filed, because the CUA will condition the approval on obtaining the license within a specified timeframe (typically 3 years per standard conditions).

items.original_text: Filing step: File the Conditional Use Authorization application with SF Planning, including the license escrow agreement, a good-neighbor operating plan, and a letter committing to comply with § 202.2 and § 249.60(d) conditions. What to say: The application narrative should frame the concept as a neighborhood wine bar with a bona fide limited kitchen, live music as a secondary amenity (not a nightclub), and a 1 a.m. closing time that respects residential neighbors. Commit in writing to (1) transfer a Type 42 license from a bar within the Mission SUD, (2) implement the § 202.2 operating conditions plus outside lighting, 33% window signage and 50% clear glazing, (3) close by 1 a.m., (4) limit live entertainment to the approved performance area, and (5) maintain the kitchen and food program. Attach the floor plan, a menu draft showing substantive food offerings, and a letter from the license broker confirming the Type 42 escrow. Request the CUA hearing be scheduled promptly; typical CUA timeline is 120–300 days per catalog entry sf.conditional_use_authorization.

items.original_text: Filing step: In parallel with the CUA, apply for the Place of Entertainment or Limited Live Performance permit with the SF Entertainment Commission, disclosing the live entertainment and amplified sound program. What to say: If live entertainment is the primary draw or the performance area exceeds 200 sq ft, file for a Place of Entertainment permit; if it is secondary and under 200 sq ft, file for Limited Live Performance. The application should state that entertainment will end by 1 a.m. (within principally permitted hours), describe the sound system and any attenuation measures (acoustic panels, sound limiters), and commit to the Entertainment Commission Good Neighbor Policy. Include the floor plan showing the performance area, the proposed entertainment schedule (how many nights per week, genre), and a security plan if POE is required. Pay the $2,708 POE application fee (FY2026–27) or the $612 LLP fee. The Entertainment Commission will route the application to Police and Planning for review; expect a 45–120 day timeline per catalog entry sf.place_of_entertainment_permit.

items.original_text: Filing step: After the CUA is granted, file the ABC Type 42 license transfer application, providing the CUA motion, the signed lease, the seller's permit, and proof of posting at the premises. What to say: Submit ABC form ABC-257 (application for transfer of license to another person and location) along with the escrow agreement, the CUA approval motion, the DBI-issued certificate of occupancy or a letter from Planning confirming zoning compliance, the CDTFA seller's permit, a 30-day public posting notice at 995 Valencia, and the transfer fee. Because the census tract is over quota, ABC will send the application to SF Planning and SFPD for a recommendation; Planning will issue a zoning clearance citing the CUA, and SFPD will review for crime and concentration issues. If SFPD or a local resident protests on undue-concentration grounds, ABC will require a Public Convenience or Necessity finding from the Board of Supervisors; coordinate with the Board's clerk to schedule the PCN hearing. The transfer takes 60–150 days if unprotested, longer if a PCN hearing is needed, per catalog entry ca.ab…

items.original_text: Filing step: File the building permit application for tenant improvements and change of use with SF Department of Building Inspection, routing it to Planning, Public Health, Fire and PUC. What to say: Submit stamped architectural plans showing the kitchen layout, hood, grease interceptor, bar, seating, restrooms, ADA path of travel, and performance area. The permit application should reference the CUA case number and state that the use is authorized by the CUA. DBI will route the plans to (1) Planning for zoning sign-off per Planning Code § 175, (2) DPH for plan check of the kitchen and bar per catalog entry sf.health_plan_check, (3) SFFD for hood suppression and occupant load, and (4) SFPUC for the grease interceptor per catalog entry sf.fog_wastewater_permit. Plan review takes 2–4 months; fees are a percentage of construction valuation, typically $800–$15,000 per catalog entry sf.building_permit. Schedule the DPH pre-opening inspection and the final DBI inspection before opening.

items.original_text: Filing step: After DPH approves the plans, file for the Health Permit to Operate, providing the Business Account Number, the certified food safety manager certificate, and the approved building permit. What to say: Apply online through the DPH portal at least one month before opening. Upload the BAN (from sf.business_registration), the Location ID, the EIN, the food safety manager's ServSafe or equivalent certificate (catalog entry ca.food_safety_manager_cert), and the DBI-approved building permit showing the kitchen layout. Pay the $470 Permit to Operate application fee (FY2026–27). DPH will schedule a pre-opening inspection; correct any deficiencies (hand sinks, hot water, sealed surfaces) before the final inspection. The permit is issued after the final inspection confirms the facility matches the approved plans. Expect 14–45 days from application to issuance per catalog entry sf.health_permit.

items.original_text: Estimated time: 120 to 300 days. Estimated government cost: $3,100 to $15,000. Notes: The timeline of 120–300 days and the cost of $3,100–$15,000 cover the Conditional Use Authorization (SF Planning Commission) and the Place of Entertainment permit (SF Entertainment Commission) when both are granted. The CUA filing fee is $3,100 (no construction) to $15,000+ (with construction cost tiers), and the POE permit application is $2,708 (FY2026–27), per catalog entries sf.conditional_use_authorization and sf.place_of_entertainment_permit. These figures do not include the ABC Type 42 license transfer cost (which is a private-market purchase, not a government fee; broker estimates run $100k–$450k in San Francisco for quota licenses, though Type 42 is non-quota and new ones are issued by ABC, so a transfer may cost less), the building permit ($800–$15,000 depending on construction valuation), the health permit ($470 application + $828–$2,207 plan check), state registrations (mostly free or under $200 total), or legal and consultant fees. The day range is the time to approval for the CUA and POE permits when they are approved; it is not the time to a denial or withdrawal. If the applicant cannot source a Type 42 license from within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD, or if Planning determines that the concept cannot satisfy the SUD's license-transfer requirement, the CUA cannot be granted and the project cannot proceed as a bar use. The records show two bar CUAs on Valencia were withdrawn or cancelled before hearing, and no pure bar use approvals in NCT-VALENCIA within 1,000 ft over the last 10 years, suggesting the pathway is constrained by the SUD rules and market availability of in-district Type 42 licenses.

The CUA filing fee is $3,100 (no construction) to $15,000+ (with construction cost tiers), and the POE permit application is $2,708 (FY2026–27), per catalog entries sf.conditional_use_authorization and sf.place_of_entertainment_permit. These figures do not include the ABC Type 42 license transfer cost (which is a private-market purchase, not a government fee; broker estimates run $100k–$450k in San Francisco for quota licenses, though Type 42 is non-quota and new ones are issued by ABC, so a transfer may cost less), the building permit ($800–$15,000 depending on construction valuation), the health permit ($470 application + $828–$2,207 plan check), state registrations (mostly free or under $200 total), or legal and consultant fees. The day range is the time to approval for the CUA and POE permits when they are approved; it is not the time to a denial or withdrawal. If the applicant cannot source a Type 42 license from within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD, or if Planning determines that the concept cannot satisfy the SUD's license-transfer requirement, the CUA cannot be granted and the project cannot proceed as a bar use. The records show two bar CUAs on Valencia were withdrawn or cancelled before hearing, and no pure bar use approvals in NCT-VALENCIA within 1,000 ft over the last 10 years, suggesting the pathway is constrained by the SUD rules and market availability of in-district Type 42 licenses.

What to say: Request a zoning determination letter or a pre-application meeting with a planner assigned to the Mission. outcomes.original: Filing step: After DPH approves the plans, file for the Health Permit to Operate, providing the Business Account Number, the certified food safety manager certificate, and the approved building permit. What to say: Apply online through the DPH portal at least one month before opening. Upload the BAN (from sf.business_registration), the Location ID, the EIN, the food safety manager's ServSafe or equivalent certificate (catalog entry ca.food_safety_manager_cert), and the DBI-approved building permit showing the kitchen layout. Pay the $470 Permit to Operate application fee (FY2026–27). DPH will schedule a pre-opening inspection; correct any deficiencies (hand sinks, hot water, sealed surfaces) before the final inspection. The permit is issued after the final inspection confirms the facility matches the approved plans. Expect 14–45 days from application to issuance per catalog entry sf.health_permit.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 120 to 300 days. Estimated government cost: $3,100 to $15,000. Notes: The timeline of 120–300 days and the cost of $3,100–$15,000 cover the Conditional Use Authorization (SF Planning Commission) and the Place of Entertainment permit (SF Entertainment Commission) when both are granted. The CUA filing fee is $3,100 (no construction) to $15,000+ (with construction cost tiers), and the POE permit application is $2,708 (FY2026–27), per catalog entries sf.conditional_use_authorization and sf.place_of_entertainment_permit. These figures do not include the ABC Type 42 license transfer cost (which is a private-market purchase, not a government fee; broker estimates run $100k–$450k in San Francisco for quota licenses, though Type 42 is non-quota and new ones are issued by ABC, so a transfer may cost less), the building permit ($800–$15,000 depending on construction valuation), the health permit ($470 application + $828–$2,207 plan check), state registrations (mostly free or under $200 total), or legal and consultant fees. The day range is the time to approval for the CUA and POE permits when they are approved; it is not the time to a denial or withdrawal. If the applicant cannot source a Type 42 license from within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD, or if Planning determines that the concept cannot satisfy the SUD's license-transfer requirement, the CUA cannot be granted and the project cannot proceed as a bar use. The records show two bar CUAs on Valencia were withdrawn or cancelled before hearing, and no pure bar use approvals in NCT-VALENCIA within 1,000 ft over the last 10 years, suggesting the pathway is constrained by the SUD rules and market availability of in-district Type 42 licenses.
